title: North Korea's AI Missile Hits 1,000 km Target
summary:
State media reported that an intermediate-range strategic projectile successfully completed a test flight into the Sea of Japan on Oct 3 under the supervision of Kim Jong Un and his family. The weapon struck a designated target 1,000 km away using artificial intelligence in its mid-course and terminal phases to correct its flight. Kim Yo Jong stated that the missile employs a maneuvering reentry vehicle capable of changing trajectory at low altitude to evade defensive systems, claiming such capabilities make the attacks unavoidable.

The 1,000 km range claimed by the Korean Central News Agency exceeds previous estimates from South Korean and Japanese officials, who reported a flight distance of 680 to 700 km. Some arms control analysts suggest the discrepancy may stem from radar blind spots during the missile's glide phase. The test occurred amid high tensions following a Sept 21 mine blast in the demilitarized zone that injured three South Korean soldiers, though U.S. Pacific Command noted the launch posed no immediate threat to U.S. territory or personnel.

U.S. Pacific Command Statement on DPRK Missile Launch

The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea launched one ballistic missile on October 03, 2026 (KST). We are aware of the missile launch and are consulting closely with our allies and partners. Based on current assessments, this event does not pose an immediate threat to U.S. personnel or territory, or to our allies. The United States remains committed to the defense of the U.S. homeland and our allies in the region.

selectedTweets.text:
North Korea says it test-fired an intermediate-range strategic missile using AI technology, capable of changing its flight path at low altitude and flying in several trajectory modes.

Kim Jong Un personally oversaw the drill. Kim Yo Jong claimed South Korea and Japan were unable to fully track the missile, saying “there is no way to avoid this attack.”

selectedTweets.text:
According to the North Korean state-run news agency KCNA, the missile tested last night was an intermediate-range ballistic missile (IRBM) that reportedly used AI in it mid-course and/or terminal phase for correction and a maneuvering reentry vehicle (MaRV), if the report is understood correctly by us. North Korean claims of AI an MaRVs during such tests is not abnormal, as such claims have been made in the past. 

Photo is of a North Korean IRBM test but not the most recent one.
